kind: repair campaign (TLSF), 2x2 factorial, all four arms from one binary
kind_note: Sweep G crosses selection_scheme (nsga2-apportion against weighted) with fitness.status_grading (mrs against aurus). Every arm runs generations = 500 under a 400 s genetic.max_wall_s, so the deadline rather than the generation count ends every run and each arm gets the same wall clock. The external harness cap is 3600 s.
question: What each arm finds as a function of time, and how the two factors interact: status_grading changes what the status objective is, and the two schemes consume that objective differently -- one of three separately ranked objectives under NSGA-II, a number scaled by 0.7 into a scalar under weighted.
endpoint: None registered. PLAN.md section 2 declares no primary endpoint, no alpha, no control arm and no decision rule. The deliverable is the six metrics of section 5.
decision_rule_firing: There is no decision rule to fire. PLAN.md section 2 registers none and says so against the practice of every other plan in this archive, which do bind one. This field is filled rather than left blank because a blank here would read as an unfinished close. Every p-value in REPORT.md and in this file is POST-HOC and labelled as such at the point it is written.

arms.shared: generations 500, max_wall_s 400, parallel 1, weights 0.1/0.2/0.7, log metric, weakening screen off, accumulate_repairs true, monolithic repair mode, run_implication true

hosts.note: The seed split comes from campaign.toml alone. Both arms of every contrast ran on one host at the same seed, so a host difference cancels inside the (spec, seed) cell.

verification.note: The two checks of PLAN.md section 12.

1_ideal_solutions_not_flat_zero.detail: implies_ideal is 184 of 600 (30.7%) and no arm is flat zero: 79/150, 83/150, 5/150 and 17/150. The compare join is sound.

2_stopped_by_reads_deadline.detail: deadline on all 355 manifests, generations on none, so no family reached 500 generations inside 400 s and the arms share a time axis.

censoring.note: A censored run wrote no manifest, so its implies_ideal reads zero in the results CSV whatever it found. The censoring is not balanced across arms -- weighted was killed on 214 of 300 paired runs against nsga2-apportion's 31 -- so the endpoint contrast between the schemes is confounded with it and only the accumulator curves separate the two.

result.headline: The weighted arms do not fail to search. They search far more prolifically and then cannot deliver. weighted/mrs accumulates 3341 gate-passing candidates a run against nsga2-apportion/mrs's 314, 10.6x more, and reports implies_ideal on 5 of 150 runs against 79. 126 of its 150 runs were killed at the 3600 s external cap.
result.mechanism: The post-deadline work is quadratic in what the search accumulated. compute_subsumed in src/filter/implication.cpp sweeps pairs over the accumulated pool at the final implication filter, so 3341 candidates is about 5.6M pairwise implication queries after the 400 s deadline has already passed -- and genetic.max_wall_s bounds the generation loop alone, interrupting neither the final realizability gate, the implication filter nor the scoring. The external cap is what ends those runs.
result.not_a_search_difference: Time to first repair is flat across all four arms: 5.6 to 6.4 s median, reached on 95.3 to 99.3 percent of runs. The schemes differ in what they accumulate and what that costs afterwards, not in how quickly they find something.
result.posthoc_selection: nsga2-apportion against weighted over 300 pairs: found_repair 191 to 9, implies_ideal 145 to 5, both exact McNemar p = 0.0000. Confounded with censoring (214 against 31 killed) and with the weights, which ride with the weighted arms by construction. POST-HOC.
result.posthoc_grading: mrs against aurus over 300 pairs: found_repair 9 to 47 in aurus's favour, p = 0.0000; implies_ideal 7 to 23, p = 0.0052; killed 146 against 99. The aurus ladder finishes more runs inside the cap. POST-HOC.

metrics_measured.solutions: all 600 runs, from the accumulator index, no solver call
metrics_measured.time_to_first_repair: all 600 runs, from the accumulator index, no solver call

owed: maximal_solutions and maximal_ideal_solutions are infeasible on this campaign's data and the arithmetic is the reason rather than the budget. The 863,531 accumulated candidates give 5,706,083,502 pairwise implication comparisons at 20 log-spaced cuts, 20.9 times the 2026-08-29 campaign, which is itself a multi-day job on two 32-core hosts. 91.7% of those candidates sit in the weighted arms, so the arm that most needs a maximality reading is the one whose reading cannot be computed. A future curve campaign that expects prolific arms should cap `accumulate_repairs` or budget for this before it launches.

close_note: Closed retroactively on 2026-09-02, four days after the runs finished. The campaign had no PROVENANCE.json and no REPORT.md, and its 600 rows and 3.5 GB of run data were found in a git worktree that had been removed, in a directory git no longer lists. Nothing was lost: git leaves ignored files behind when it removes a worktree. The data now sits in the main checkout's experiments/ beside every other campaign's.

ideal_reach.note: The first owed item, discharged on 2026-09-03. It settles the censoring confound the close flagged, and it settles it against the recorded endpoint: on what the accumulator holds, the two factors are indistinguishable.

paired_tests.note: Paired on the (spec, seed) cell, 150 cells per arm, with any pair holding an undecided run held out per PLAN.md section 6. POST-HOC, as every test in this file is: PLAN.md registers no endpoint and no decision rule.
paired_tests.selection_pooled: nsga2-apportion against weighted, 14 to 18 over 277 pairs (23 held out), exact McNemar p = 0.5966
paired_tests.grading_pooled: mrs against aurus, 15 to 7 over 281 pairs (19 held out), exact McNemar p = 0.1338
paired_tests.selection_within_mrs: 8 to 11 over 137 pairs (13 held out), p = 0.6476
paired_tests.selection_within_aurus: 6 to 7 over 140 pairs (10 held out), p = 1.0000
paired_tests.grading_within_nsga2_apportion: 6 to 3 over 144 pairs (6 held out), p = 0.5078
paired_tests.grading_within_weighted: 9 to 4 over 137 pairs (13 held out), p = 0.2668
paired_tests.folded_in_alternative: Folding the undecided in as failures gives selection 19 to 19 over 300 (p = 1.0000) and grading 16 to 10 over 300 (p = 0.3269). Recorded because it is what a reader who skips section 6 will compute, and because it changes no conclusion here.

ideal_reach.correction_to_the_recorded_endpoint: section_5_measures and per_family_implies_ideal read implies_ideal off the results CSV, which records what a run REPORTED inside the 3600 s external cap. 245 of 600 runs were killed before they reported anything, 214 of them in the weighted arms, and the close recorded that as a confound. This metric scores what the accumulator HELD instead, and the confound accounts for the whole effect: the recorded 145-to-5 selection contrast (p = 0.0000) becomes 14-to-18 (p = 0.5966). Every family whose recorded weighted implies_ideal was flat zero -- detector-aurus, lily02, lily11, ltl2dba-r-2, ltl2dba-theta-2, ltl2dba27, rg2, round-robin-arbiter-aurus, simple-arbiter-aurus -- reads 6/6 here on at least one weighted arm. lily15 reverses outright, the weighted arms reading 4/6 and 5/6 against nsga2-apportion's 1/6 and 0/6.
ideal_reach.what_this_does_and_does_not_change: REPORT.md's mechanism stands unchanged and is now the whole story: the post-deadline implication filter is quadratic in what the search accumulated, genetic.max_wall_s does not bound it, and the weighted arms accumulate 10.6x more. What does not stand is any reading of the recorded implies_ideal as a difference in what the schemes FIND. Time to first ideal repair is flat at 5.7 to 7.1 s across all four arms, matching the flat time to first repair already recorded. The schemes differ in delivery, not in reach.

scored_by.where: This workstation rather than av2 or av3, both hosts being committed to the 2026-08-29 campaign's maximality pass when this ran. Five workers of four cores under `nice -n 15`, inside a cgroup v2 scope capped at MemoryHigh=12G / MemoryMax=16G / MemorySwapMax=0, the box having 30 GB against the lab machines' 125 GB and `compare` spawning ltlfilt children measured into the gigabytes. Nothing was killed by the cap.

scorer.note: Byte-identical to this directory's vendored copy under scripts/, verified with git hash-object, so the pass ran the archived scorer rather than a later one.

compare_binary.why_dirty: Built in a worktree carrying unrelated in-progress work on the FRETISH implication query. `src/compare.cpp` is byte-identical between a10ecbc and this campaign's own 96c3311, so the driver is the one the campaign would have used.
compare_binary.carried_a_tlsf_reduction: The binary linked an experimental cancellation of the TLSF implication query, since dropped. `compare` classifies a repair against an ideal through tlsf_spec_implies, which that cancellation sat behind, so it is load-bearing here and is recorded rather than glossed. The reduction is exact by construction, every step being an equivalence, and it had already been checked against `maximal` -- which calls the same tlsf_spec_implies -- over 1,108 specifications from the 2026-08-29 campaign with byte-identical results.

verification.what: A sample of this campaign's own runs re-scored with a `compare` built from the reverted tree, whose tlsf_spec_implies is byte-identical to a10ecbc's, and the CSVs compared byte for byte against the archived ones. Any difference would be a verdict the reduction moved.
verification.sample: 20 runs, five per arm, spread over the accumulated-set size range and drawn only from runs that reached an ideal, an empty ideal set exercising no implication query at all.
verification.conclusion: The reduction changed no verdict on this campaign's data.

undecided_runs.note: compare timed out before it could rank what the run held, so whether it reached an ideal-implying candidate is unknown. PLAN.md section 6 distinguishes this third state from censoring and forbids folding it into it. Every paired test below holds a pair out where either side is undecided.
undecided_runs.why_it_matters: The count tracks the accumulated pool size that makes a compare call slow, so it falls on the prolific arms. Folding the 32 in as failures charges weighted for its own slow scoring; done that way the two factors read 19 to 19 (p = 1.0000) and 16 to 10 (p = 0.3269). Both readings are flat here so no conclusion turns on it, and in a campaign whose contrast is not flat it would.

compare_provenance.not_the_campaign_binary: The campaign itself ran at 1816e27. compare_provenance.why_it_is_nonetheless_sound: The campaign's own binary computed implies_ideal per run at 1816e27, and on the 355 runs that reported a manifest the accumulator-derived reach from this newer compare agrees with it 355 of 355, with no disagreement in either direction. That is the cross-check PLAN.md section 12 asks for, and it is what licenses the newer binary here.

Verified against this branch: the only example directory that differs anywhere under examples/ is mode-arbiter, a FRETISH subject outside this campaign's 25-family TLSF corpus, so every ideal set used is byte-identical to the campaign branch's.

verification_3_accumulator_agrees_with_e.detail: On the 355 runs that were not killed at the cap and whose compare call decided, accumulator-derived ideal reach equals the results CSV's implies_ideal on 355 of 355. Of the 245 killed runs, 160 had already found an ideal-implying candidate, 53 had not, and 32 are undecided.
